content:
SmartGym today released a major update, introducing AI-powered workout plan creation and management features, deeper Siri integration, and a range of features that take advantage of new possibilities in iOS 27, iPadOS, and watchOS 27. Here are the details.

I've previously written about how much I enjoy using SmartGym to log my fitness habits.

SmartGym is an Apple Design Award winner, and the reasons why are obvious. Developer Matt Abras keeps improving, updating, and refining the app to make managing, tracking, and logging workouts easier and smoother. This long-standing entry among the most polished and practical fitness trackers on the App Store continues to get better and better.

Today, SmartGym rolls out one of its biggest updates ever. SmartGym 8 introduces "SmartGym Intelligence," essentially the app's own version of Private Cloud Compute.

SmartGym rolls out its own Private Cloud Compute alternative

As Abras explains, SmartGym currently doesn't qualify for Apple Private Cloud Compute, which is offered through the new Foundation Models framework. So he decided to build his own solution.

SmartGym 8 leverages Apple's new Language Model API to extend the Foundation Models framework to cutting-edge models running on SmartGym's own private cloud infrastructure, while keeping requests anonymous and fully decoupled from user identity.

With today's update, users can now create workout plans using natural language. That means they can type something like "build me a push-pull-legs split with 10 exercises per day, avoid bench press, and add 2 warm-up exercises each day," and the app's new framework handles the rest.

Once a workout plan is created, users can send follow-up instructions to fine-tune things, such as "move my leg day to Friday," "remove barbell squats," or "set Wednesday as a rest day."

To try out the new SmartGym Intelligence, users can open the "Workouts" tab in SmartGym 8 on iPhone and iPad, tap the + button, and type in what they need. On Apple Watch, users simply open the app, scroll down on the main screen, tap "Add Workout," choose "Just Say It," and describe what they want.

SmartGym + Siri AI

SmartGym 8 also taps into the new Siri AI rolling out with today's 2027 OS updates. Abras says:

Users can now not only control an in-progress workout with commands like "SmartGym next exercise" or "log a set in SmartGym," but also launch SmartGym workouts directly from Siri.

With SmartGym's data accessible to Siri, users can also ask questions like "What workouts do I have planned in SmartGym this week?" or "Show me my dumbbell workouts in SmartGym" — the integration doesn't just surface the relevant information, but actually presents rich visual results right in the Siri interface.

The same integration works for specific workout details, such as "show me my heart rate history in SmartGym," as well as creating new exercises.

Users can also use the new Siri AI to create entirely new workout plans in natural language, either by typing or speaking. Siri AI and SmartGym then take over from there, creating and organising a new workout programme based on the instruction.

Finally, SmartGym 8 also takes advantage of Siri's new on-screen awareness, which is incredibly handy during a workout. Users can ask Siri to identify what's on screen, answer questions about it, or say "open the third workout plan on screen" to jump straight to it without ever touching the device. Users can also start from an image — particularly handy when you've received a written plan from a personal trainer.

Other details

SmartGym 8 packs in plenty more. That includes:

  • Exercise Q&A with images: SmartGym can now feed exercise demonstration images into the Foundation Models running on-device on Apple devices, for better, more detailed answers about individual exercises.
  • Resizable interface: The app's interface now adapts more dynamically to different window sizes, orientations, and screen shapes, in preparation for the new iPhone Duo.
  • More Liquid Glass design: SmartGym extends the Liquid Glass design to more parts of the app, including segmented controls, the muscle group selector, alert sheets, and the duration timer.

SmartGym is available as a free download on the App Store, with a range of subscription options.
